scope: Focused actual-source image inspection and read-only topology QA; no game edits

findings.observation: The source image visibly depicts a pond-like widened water body toward the upper interior and a narrow channel descending toward the lower edge. The new fixture places river_ns north and pond_small south; this pairing appears directionally suspect. In particular pond_small itself is an isolated pool with grass on the outer edges.
findings.implication: Do not accept pond_channel_s_N_to_river_S and pond_channel_s_S_to_pond_N as validated; check actual 24px edge water runs and reverse/alternative layouts before adopting.

findings.observation: The tile is visually asymmetric rather than an obvious four-way canonical EW-road/NS-rail crossing; its visible road/track layout requires edge-direction identification.
findings.implication: The crossing_basic fixture currently assumes EW road and NS rail on all four sides; do not certify its neighbor assignment without edge classification and game-source confirmation.

findings.observation: Barrier and track/road markings differ substantially from crossing_basic; the same neighbor assignment is not proven for both variants.
findings.implication: Keep the closed variant as a distinct candidate; do not infer identical connection mask solely from the word crossing.

findings.observation: The two EW bridge sprites show a horizontal deck over blue water and different approach-side background from ordinary straight road/rail tiles. The 2026-11-12 RGB edge MAE is elevated, but the cause cannot be diagnosed from a single sprite alone.
findings.implication: Review individual 24px multi-tile composites; do not claim an image defect or approve continuity from MAE alone.

source_sha_verification: Actual PNGs were read through GitHub connector; source SHAs matched the previously recorded manifest for visually examined examples. The new script will independently verify blobs when run in a checkout.
